# JVM secure coding

- Use prepared/bound parameters for JDBC, JPA/JPQL, native queries, and search/filter expressions. Map dynamic identifiers and sort fields to fixed values.
- Never deserialize untrusted Java/native objects with `ObjectInputStream`, XMLDecoder, unsafe Kryo, or type-enabled JSON/YAML. Prefer schema-validated DTOs; an object filter is defense in depth, not a reason to accept native objects.
- Configure XML factories to disallow DTDs/external entities and external schema/stylesheet access. Set parser size and depth limits.
- Do not pass untrusted values to JNDI lookups, SpEL/OGNL/MVEL expressions, script engines, reflection class loading, or dynamic templates.
- Launch a fixed executable with `ProcessBuilder` argument elements and no shell. Validate option-like inputs and apply time/output limits.
- Use `SecureRandom` for security values and standard JCA/JCE high-level constructions. Do not select weak algorithms, accept all certificates/hostnames, or embed key material.
- Keep validation on request DTOs and authorization in service/resource policy. Do not expose persistence entities for automatic binding or trust client owner/role fields.
- Preserve output encoding in JSP/Thymeleaf/template engines; avoid raw/unescaped output and user-controlled view/template names.
- Use `Path.normalize`/`toRealPath` as appropriate and verify confinement under an intended base. Account for symlinks and create files safely.
- Bound streams, collections, decompression, regex, thread pools, queues, and remote calls. Set connect/read/request timeouts and propagate cancellation/interruption.
- Do not expose verbose exceptions or enable management/debug endpoints publicly. Keep secrets out of properties, annotations, logs, heap-dump endpoints, and client-visible configuration.
- Keep compiler null-safety/static-analysis checks and dependency verification enabled. Avoid broad suppression and insecure trust-manager examples.
